PullRequest.Title: Toolbar: items that always show, and fix Reset Menu duplication
PullRequest.Body:

## Problem

`WorkbenchToolBar` lets users hide items of a toolbar from its context menu, but there is no way to keep some items of such a toolbar always shown. A feature that owns a customizable toolbar (for example the title bar of an editor area it arranges) needs a few fixed items, such as a close or layout button, while the user can still show or hide the others.

The context menu also has a latent bug that such fixed items expose. `Separator.join(primaryActions, toggleActions)` returns the `toggleActions` array itself when `primaryActions` is empty. The toolbar then pushes a separator and "Reset Menu" onto that array, and the array lives as long as the toolbar's current set of actions. So every right-click appends another "Reset Menu". On `main` today the primary list is never empty when there are toggle actions, because the menu always gets a "Hide …" or "Configure Keybinding" entry, so the bug does not show yet. It shows as soon as an item has no entries of its own, which is what an always-shown submenu is.

Repro (with the API below, before the copy fix): a toolbar with `hiddenItemStrategy: HiddenItemStrategy.Ignore`, a `resetMenu`, a hidden item, and an always-shown submenu. Right-click the always-shown submenu twice: the second menu lists "Reset Menu" twice, the third three times, and so on.

## Fix

- New `IWorkbenchToolBarOptions.alwaysShownItems?: readonly string[]`: items of the primary group, by command id or, for submenus, by submenu id, that cannot be hidden. They always show, even if the user hid them before (a stored hidden state is ignored). They are not listed among the items that can be shown or hidden, and they do not count as the last item that cannot be hidden, so the other items can all be hidden. Right-clicking one of them lists the items that can be shown or hidden.
- The context menu now copies the result of `Separator.join` (`[...Separator.join(primaryActions, toggleActions)]`) before adding "Reset Menu", so the toggle actions are never modified.

No existing toolbar sets `alwaysShownItems`, and the copy only matters when the primary list is empty, so existing toolbars behave as before.

## How to test

Unit tests in `src/vs/platform/actions/test/browser/toolbar.test.ts`:
- "items that always show cannot be hidden, and list the items that can be": the always-shown submenu shows, its context menu lists only the items that can be shown or hidden plus "Reset Menu", the same on a second right-click (the duplication), and the last optional item can be hidden.
- "items that always show ignore a hidden state stored for them": an always-shown item that was hidden keeps showing and is not listed in the context menu.

Manually, a toolbar would need to set the option; nothing in `main` does yet.

## Validation

On `agents/toolbar-always-shown-items-main` (two commits on `origin/main` d2e7f610b88):
- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts src/vs/platform/actions/browser/toolbar.ts src/vs/platform/actions/test/browser/toolbar.test.ts`: passed (2 files).
- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/vs/platform/actions/browser/toolbar.ts src/vs/platform/actions/test/browser/toolbar.test.ts`: passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only && ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/actions/test/browser/toolbar.test.ts`: 4 passing.
- Red check, the `[...Separator.join(...)]` copy reverted (alwaysShownItems kept): the first new test fails with "Reset Menu" repeated in the second context menu. Restored: 4 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "vs/platform/actions/test/**/*.test.js"`: 36 passing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Menu-backed or manually populated toolbar creation and updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A menu-change event (debounced where configured) or direct caller synchronously enters WorkbenchToolBar.setActions, classifies primary actions, then calls the base toolbar to rebuild action view items/DOM before the toolbar update completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Primary toolbar action count N and configured alwaysShownItems count K. The new membership check is O(N*K) only when the new option is configured; no production caller in the changed repository configures it, and realistic toolbars have a small bounded number of actions and fixed items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Toolbar updates execute serially on the UI JavaScript thread; MenuWorkbenchToolBar uses the menu service's existing debounce and introduces no new queue, fan-out, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or remote lookup is added. The readonly option is reused for each update, and existing menu/action state supplies hidden flags. Cold and warm behavior differ only through pre-existing menu state; there are no misses, negative-cache retries, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed loop and includes scan are direct, and repository search establishes that only tests opt into the option. The added no-option function/type check is constant work per already-processed action.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future consumers could provide larger arrays, but this is an internal toolbar API and the expected action/fixed-item cardinalities are small; there are currently no non-test consumers of alwaysShownItems.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed action classification is synchronous but bounded, adds no expensive boundary, and existing production toolbars do not opt into the only scaling scan.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a customizable toolbar context menu, including repeated right-clicks on an always-shown item
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user contextmenu event synchronously resolves the clicked action, builds configure/hide/toggle entries, shallow-copies the joined action list, appends Reset Menu when applicable, and hands the list to the context-menu service for rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of toggle actions in that toolbar. The spread copies one small action-reference array once per user-triggered context-menu open; it does not clone actions or traverse unrelated menus.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous UI event at a time on the renderer thread; context menus are user-triggered and no asynchronous tasks or concurrent boundary operations are launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Toggle actions are captured from the most recent setActions call. The new copy prevents the cached toggleActions array from being mutated by Reset Menu entries, so repeated opens remain constant-size rather than retaining one separator/action pair per open. No cold/warm cache or negative-cache behavior applies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Separator.join aliasing and the shallow spread are explicit in the changed hunk and covered by the added repeated-open test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact toolbar action counts vary, but context menus are typically small and manually triggered. The prior mutation condition was not reachable by existing production configurations according to the code search; it becomes reachable with the new always-shown option and is prevented in the same diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The one bounded allocation per open is negligible and prevents unbounded repeated-menu growth in the newly enabled scenario; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call is added or moved onto the path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced toolbar update/render and context-menu-open paths, checked existing option consumers, action cardinality, UI-thread scheduling, retention behavior, and transitive expensive boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found, and the PR does not qualify as a shipped-regression fix because the old aliasing path was not reachable in existing production configurations.
